news.title: Meet the Press NOW — July 28
news.description: A solemn day in Washington as President Trump and world leaders attend the late Senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral. Documentary filmmaker Alex Holder spent over four years with Senator Lindsey Graham right until his death and shares never-before-seen footage with Meet the Press NOW. In Michigan, Congresswoman Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) and Abdul El-Sayed (D) had their final debate last night in the closely watched race, with just one week to go before the primary.

news.title: ‘I’m tired’: Lindsey Graham in never-before-seen video as he tried to secure deal to end Ukraine war
news.description: Meet the Press moderator Kristen Welker sits down with documentary filmmaker Alex Holder who spent more four years following Senator Graham right until his death. Holder shares never-before-seen footage of Senator Graham raising concerns about “war fatigue” in Ukraine and a conversation between Lindsey and his sister Darline Graham about his entry into politics.

news.title: Netanyahu & Zelenskyy attend Graham funeral as wars in Iran and Ukraine reach critical points
news.description: President Trump, lawmakers, and world leaders attend Sen. Lindsey Graham’s funeral as policymakers try to navigate a path forward in the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Elise Labott, host of the Cosmopolitics podcast, discusses where the U.S. stands in the Iran War as it enters its sixth month and the administration’s evolving relationship with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy.

news.description: Maine Democrats have selected Troy Jackson as their new Senate candidate after former nominee Anthony Platner withdrew amid controversy. Yes — they are saying he may NOT be eligible, but that is a legal challenge, not a settled fact.

The argument comes from a Maine election-law issue: a Republican state lawmaker asked the Maine Secretary of State to review whether Troy Jackson can become the Democratic U.S. Senate nominee because Jackson had previously run in another 2026 race (the Maine governor’s race primary). The claim is that Maine law may restrict someone who already participated in one primary from becoming a replacement nominee for a different office.

However:

* Maine Democrats did select Troy Jackson as their Senate nominee by convention.

* He has not been ruled ineligible by the state.
* The issue is about Maine election law and the replacement-nomination process, not the U.S. Constitution’s Senate requirements.

So the accurate answer is:

Yes, Troy Jackson is currently eligible to run unless Maine election officials or courts decide otherwise. The people saying “he can’t run” are referring to a challenge/argument, not a final decision.

It’s similar to many election disputes: someone can be on the ballot while a legal question is being fought.
